answer: Voting and settlement capacity accrue only to a hardware-rooted key that repeatedly solves a sequential puzzle chained to the last finalized hash. When many keys share a network ridge—identical ASN, clock skew, or runtime digest—the protocol merges their capacity into one bucket and raises puzzle cost with the size of the cluster. Those merged inventories are notarized under a cedar checkpoint published each hour, and a public beacon repeats the cluster list so counterparties can refuse clone-farms before funds move.
